> > I was wondering if it would be possible to search a trace (or a neuron ID from flycircuit) in registered Gal4s. Also, would it be possible to define a certain space in the brain and find all the registered Gal4s that have GFP expression there?
>
> We have a prototype version of the functionality to search flycircuit ids against Gal4 lines. If you contact me directly, I can provide further details. We would be pleased to get feedback on our test version.

Further to this we now have a live online version of this Gal4 search available here:

http://flybrain.mrc-lmb.cam.ac.uk:8080/NBLAST_on-the-fly/

Best wishes,

Greg.

messages.subject: Re: Questions about image registration
messages.body_plain:
Hi Tetsuya,

On 10 Feb 2016, at 11:46, Tetsuya Nojima wrote:

> I am Tetsuya Nojima, a post-doc of Stephen Goodwin's lab at the
> University of Oxford.

Nice to hear from you.

> I'm writing to you to ask questions about the image registration
> reported in Cachero et al., 2010.
> I would like to learn how to make an average intersex template brain.
> Although I have carefully read your papers and some previous studies,
> I couldn't find it.
> I found this web page http://bit.ly/1QevBoE and guess this page
> contains all information needed to make an average template brain, but
> probably due to the lack of knowledge and skills of mine, I still
> can't.
> Could you please send me the detailed instruction manual if available
> or teach me how to do it?

I'm afraid making average brains is a little more complicated because it
is an iterative process with multiple rounds of two registration tools.
The script on github that you have found is the primary documentation.
However, it only works in a quite specific compute environment, which
particular programs available (CMTK of course, but also Sun Grid
Engine). If it looks too complicated for you to adapt, you can send your
brains and we could try to do this for you, although I can't really
promise a timeline – someone in my lab would need to do it with help
from me.

> Apart from this, I'm also struggling to understand what the
> "Registration Params" is, which I can see when I open the window "CMTK
> Registration GUI" by going to Fiji > Plugins > CMTK Registration >
> CMTK Registration GUI.

These are additional parameters to customise the registration. The full
details are here:

http://flybrain.mrc-lmb.cam.ac.uk/dokuwiki/doku.php?id=warping_manual:registration_parameters

But you just need to choose Registration Params "Cachero, Ostrovsky
2010"

> I'm wondering whether the knowledge of programming is required to
> understand these things.

To run the registration using that GUI, you do not need To modify/run
the average brain script, you would need some knowledge of shell
scripting and a very little R.

All the best,

Greg.
